findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — [P1, confidence 100] `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource's generated ID into a lookup by group-ID name, so every per-group member-view grant falls back to the all-groups resource and user searches/counts omit the members of groups granted individually.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1 confidence 100: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource ID to a lookup that requires the group ID/name, so every per-group VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant falls back to the all-groups resource and user search/count omits the permitted group's members.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1 (confidence 100): `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource UUID to `findByName` instead of its group-ID name, so a caller granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on an individual group receives an empty permitted-group set and user search/count endpoints silently return no eligible group members unless an all-groups policy happens to exist.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — [P1, confidence 100] `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` treats the all-groups `view` scope as `manage`, so a view-only administrator passes `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`'s `requireManage()` check and creates or reparents groups without write authorization.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — [P1/100] The suite stays green while the verbatim `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` lets an all-groups `view` grant create and mutate groups, because `testManageAllGroups` exercises only `Set.of(MANAGE)` and never asserts that a view-only grant is forbidden from those mutations.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:306 — [P2/75] The verbatim `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` is never followed by a membership read assertion, so the test passes when the endpoint accepts the request but leaves Bob out of the group.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — P1 confidence 100: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes the authorization resource ID to a lookup that requires the group ID/name, so every per-group VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant falls back to the all-groups resource and user search/count omits the permitted group's members.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in GroupPermissionsV2.java line 122, the method `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates over resources and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However, examining the `hasPermission` method (lines 130-157), when a non-null groupId is passed, it does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` to look up the resource. The issue is that `groupResource.getId()` returns the authorization resource's internal ID, but `findByName` expects the group's actual ID (which is used as the resource name, as seen in AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId()). This mismatch means the lookup will fail to find the resource, causing it to fall back to the all-groups resource type check, which defeats the purpose of per-group permission checking.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 115-125, the `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` method iterates over resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However, examining the `hasPermission` method at lines 131-157, when a non-null groupId is passed, it calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` at line 143. The issue is that `groupResource.getId()` returns the authorization resource's UUID, but `findByName` expects the group's ID as the resource name (as seen in `resolveGroup` which returns `group.getId()` as the name). This mismatch means the lookup will fail to find the resource, causing the permission check to fall back to the type-level resource check, which may not grant the expected permissions for individual group members.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a legitimate test coverage gap. Looking at the diff, `canManage()` in GroupPermissionsV2.java (line 70) returns true if the user has VIEW or MANAGE permission on all-groups (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). This means a VIEW-only permission would allow `canManage()` to return true, which seems incorrect - VIEW should not grant MANAGE capabilities. The test `testManageAllGroups` only tests with `Set.of(MANAGE)` and doesn't verify that a VIEW-only grant is properly forbidden from mutations. This is a valid test coverage concern for newly added permission logic, though it's not necessarily a bug since the implementation may be intentional (allowing VIEW to imply some management capabilities).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test `testManageGroupMembership` calls `joinGroup(topGroup.getId())` but never verifies that Bob was actually added to the group. Looking at the diff, the test only checks that the call doesn't throw an exception (via the earlier `fail()` pattern), but doesn't assert the membership was created. This is a legitimate test quality concern - the test verifies permission checking works but not that the actual operation succeeds. However, this is not a bug in the production code, just an incomplete test assertion.
